# `m.futures.bars`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Open, high, low, close, and volume bars of futures contracts.

```python
m.futures.bars(symbols, timespan, *, multiplier=1, venues=frozenset(dm.FuturesVenue))
```

| Methods | `blink()`, `append_only()`, `ring()`, `last_by()`, `history()` |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Contract tickers, a contracts table, or `dm.ALL`. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and each one you delete stops being read. `last_by()`, `fetch()`, `history()`, and most polls also drop a deleted symbol's rows. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; by default, a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |
| `timespan` | The bar's unit, any but `dm.Timespan.DAY`. | The unit of each bar, a `dm.Timespan` member: `SECOND`, `MINUTE`, `HOUR`, `DAY`, `WEEK`, `MONTH`, `QUARTER`, or `YEAR`; futures take `SESSION` in place of `DAY`. Text such as `"day"` raises `TypeError`: write `dm.Timespan.DAY`, or convert text with `dm.Timespan("day")`. One-second and one-minute bars with `multiplier=1` also stream; every other length is history only. |
| `multiplier` | Units per bar. | How many `timespan` units each bar spans; the default is 1. `timespan=dm.Timespan.MINUTE, multiplier=5` gives five-minute bars. |
| `venues` | The exchanges whose flat files `history()` reads. | The exchanges whose futures flat files `history()` reads, as a set of `dm.FuturesVenue` members: `CME`, `CBOT`, `NYMEX`, and `COMEX`; the default is all four. Massive sells futures flat files by exchange, so pass the ones your plan holds. Streams and REST reads ignore it. |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `ticker`: "The ticker for the contract."; flat files `ticker`: "The exchange symbol that this item is traded under."; WebSocket `sym`: "The ticker symbol for the given future." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Date` | String | The futures session of the bar (its trading date), as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: Massive's `session_end_date` from REST and the flat files, and on the WebSocket the session as for futures trades; null for a bar of several sessions, a week or longer, or an intraday bar that crosses 17:00 Chicago time. Joining an intraday row to the same day's daily bar on `Date` attaches values not known until that day ended, and a null `Date` matches another null, so join longer bars on `TimestampEnd`. From REST `session_end_date`: "Also known as the trading date, the date of the end of the trading session, in YYYY-MM-DD format. Sessions are named by this end date, while window_start holds the session's start date, which for session candles is the day before."; flat files `session_end_date`: "Also known as the trading date, the date of the end of the trading session, in YYYY-MM-DD format." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `TimestampStart` | Instant | The start of the bar's window, as an Instant: Massive's own window start. From REST `window_start`: "The timestamp of the beginning of the candlestick’s aggregation window."; flat files `window_start`: "The Unix nanosecond timestamp for the start of the aggregate window."; WebSocket `s`: "The start timestamp of this aggregate window in Unix Milliseconds." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `TimestampEnd` | Instant | The exclusive end of the bar's window, as an Instant: the first instant at which the bar is complete, so an as-of join on it, `t.aj(bars, on=["Symbol", "Timestamp>=TimestampEnd"])`, never attaches a bar that is still open. It is when the window closes, not when Massive published the bar, and Massive may correct a bar later. An intraday bar ends its length after its start (a one-second WebSocket bar at Massive's `e` as sent, with a WARNING when that is not one second after its start); a bar of a session or longer at 17:00 Chicago time on its label, Massive's `session_end_date`, which is its last session. history() returns a bar of several sessions, or of a week or longer, only once no later session can still join it. A row read before its window ended has `TimestampInsert` before `TimestampEnd`, and its values can still change; `t.where("TimestampEnd <= TimestampInsert")` keeps only the rows read after their window ended. That test reads the local clock, which can be off, and a row read within moments of its end, or from a delayed feed, may still lack the window's last trades; an end set later than the window's (an index day's extra hour, a stamp kept as sent) only keeps a finished row out longer. A bar of several sessions or longer read before its last session passes that test once its latest session so far has ended, though later sessions can still join it. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Open` | double | The opening price within the timeframe. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `High` | double | The highest price within the timeframe. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Low` | double | The lowest price within the timeframe. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Close` | double | The last price within the timeframe. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Volume` | double | The number of contracts that traded within the timeframe. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Transactions` | long | The number of transactions that occurred within the timeframe. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `DollarVolume` | double | The sum of price × size across all trades in the window, expressed in the contract's quoted price units, which are the same units as the bar's open, high, low, and close. Despite the field name, no contract multiplier is applied, so this is not a notional dollar value. See the Products endpoint (https://massive.com/docs/rest/futures/products) for contract multiplier details. Because dollar_volume is a raw sum, you can use it to compute a volume-weighted average price (VWAP) over any span of bars: sum dollar_volume across the bars in the window and divide by the summed volume. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `SettlementPrice` | double | The price the contract settled at for this session. Included for session, week, month, quarter, and year candles; for multi-session candles it is the settlement of the final session in the period. Not returned for intraday candles (sec, min, hour). | REST, flat files |
| `Exchange` | long | The exchange ID. See Exchanges (https://massive.com/docs/rest/futures/market-operations/exchanges) for Massive's mapping of exchange IDs. | flat files |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
